astronaut.recognizable_1x: Yes, instantly: face, smile, hair, neck ring, mission patch, helmet on right, shuttle upper right, flag stripes at left all read. But it reads as a sepia/olive woodcut, not the photo.
astronaut.dynamic_range: Severely compressed. Luminance regression vs target (12px box) slope 0.21 (corr 0.77 egypt / 0.81 six). Main subject regions span only L~49-95: face target (203,167,143) -> (122,95,58); grey backdrop (169,157,143) -> (100,82,48); orange suit (204,83,48) -> (132,90,56); black neck (10,6,4) -> (60,59,30); helmet black (48,47,47) -> (77,68,38). No whites anywhere (shuttle, flag white stripes, helmet highlight, patch rim are tan), and blacks are lifted by the fixed tan interstitial (~10-20% of area) between dots.
astronaut.edges: Strong point. Oriented half-split (wedge) fields draw sub-dot edges: helmet rim crescent (right), collar ring, flag stripe diagonals (left), shuttle silhouette, patch outline, smile and eyes. Some contours look over-outlined (dark wedge chains).
astronaut.color: Gamut limited to tan/brown/olive/dark green. Suit not orange, flag red (129,17,25) -> tan (105,74,44), flag blue -> olive, grey backdrop -> brown; hair gets green flecks (worse in six_basins).
astronaut.egypt_vs_six: six_basins marginally stronger by luminance tracking (corr 0.809 vs 0.768; MAE 60.6 vs 61.0) with slightly smoother dark steps in neck/helmet, but mean color is identical ((100,79,48) vs (100,80,47)); it adds green speckles in the hair crown and does not add any new hue the image needs (orange, red, white, blue, grey). The extra basins essentially failed to widen the palette.
astronaut.zoom_10x: Dots are real, mostly crisp farms with coordinate/diameter labels; rings, hubs, spokes, wedge sectors visible; no repeated stamp within a crop; colors look untinted. Defects: (1) all fields drawn at one size, so small fields (143-191 m, e.g. 22.729,31.548 143 m; 22.865,31.880 165 m amorphous blur; 22.703,31.195 189 m) are upsampled ~2.5-3x and soft/blocky next to crisp 400 m fields; (2) dots sit on a flat tan fill with a soft dark/light halo around each disc, very visible in dark regions (zoom1) as a bright honeycomb; (3) some admitted Egyptian fields contain off-field ground inside the circle (22.583,28.421 372 m: white bare land and a building, used in both solves; 22.965,31.434: bright margin + dark band); (4) the same field lands in the same cell in both solves (e.g. 22.765,31.399; 23.131,31.488), and very few foreign fields appear even in six_basins (Al Jawf 30.287,38.814; Columbia 45.885,-119.123; Bahia -12.060,-45.502).

toshka.recognizable_1x: Yes for the macro geography: lake lobes NW and SE, the canal running SE from the lake center, desert vs farmland split. No for the defining content: the target's own pivot circles.
toshka.dynamic_range: Luminance slope 0.53 (corr 0.95 egypt / 0.96 six). Desert too dark and desaturated: southern desert target (213,143,84) -> dots (154,107,69), i.e. the dots are darker than the tan gap between them; lake target (27,31,22) -> (58,55,30), blacks doubled by tan gaps.
toshka.edges: Lake shorelines and the canal are crisp (wedge fields chain along the canal as a thin dark line), a real strength. But inside the farm clusters the target's dark pivots (same size as a composite dot) are rendered as randomly-oriented dark half-moons over mid-brown full discs: a fish-scale mottle instead of discrete dark circles on bright sand.
toshka.color: Target sand is saturated orange; composite is muted tan/pink-brown. six_basins introduces mauve-grey discs (Texas 36.090,-102.634; Al Jawf 30.x,38.x) in the eastern and northern desert, adding a grey cast and blotchiness.
toshka.egypt_vs_six: six_basins marginally better on luminance correlation (0.964 vs 0.950; MAE 26.2 vs 26.7) and slightly more dark-tone variety in fields, but its foreign fields add off-hue grey/mauve discs in the desert; egypt_only desert reads more uniformly as Egyptian sand. Net: roughly a wash, slight numeric edge to six_basins.
toshka.zoom_10x: Real, crisp fields with coherent wedge orientation along edges (zoom0 diagonal of half-dark/half-tan fields). Defects: small fields upsampled (22.751,31.161 191 m; 22.880,31.532 182 m) are soft; irregular non-circular crop boundaries inside some admitted circles (22.638,31.374 272 m with white irregular blob; 22.771,31.367); the Texas fallow disc 36.090,-102.634 is a flat featureless mauve disc; flat tan interstitial with soft halos everywhere.

primary_gap: Tonal/colour gamut ceiling: the composites cannot reach the target's light and saturated tones. The brightest fields the solver ever places are ~L110-120 sand/fallow discs, so everything brighter (face, white shuttle and flag stripes, grey backdrop, orange suit, Toshka's orange sand) collapses into one tan band, while lifted blacks from the tan interstitial squeeze the bottom. Astronaut luminance slope is 0.21 and Toshka 0.53; adding four basins left mean colour unchanged, so the bank has no bright, near-white, saturated orange/red, neutral-grey or bluish fields.
gap_secondary: solver/compositor: fixed tan interstitial between dots lifts black level (lake L 58 vs 27; neck 60 vs ~7) and draws a bright honeycomb in dark areas; single draw size forces small fields to be upsampled; absolute colour matching with no tone mapping clips all tones above the palette ceiling.
acceptance_condition: Measured on the 1x composites at 892 px against the target resized to match, with dot interiors only (gap pixels excluded) and fields left unaltered (no gain, tint or curve applied to field pixels, verified at 10x): (a) astronaut 12px-box luminance regression slope >= 0.45 (now 0.21) and Pearson >= 0.85 (now 0.81); (b) astronaut face box (x350-420, y170-230) dot-interior mean L >= 140 (now ~92) and the suit box (x120-220, y620-720) has mean R-B >= 90 (now ~77); (c) Toshka southern desert box (x250-500, y760-840) dot-interior mean within 25 RGB units per channel of target (213,143,84) (now (154,107,69)); (d) lake box (x130-330, y60-200) whole-pixel mean L <= 40 (now 48) once gaps are counted; (e) at 10x every visible dot still shows real farm structure with legible coordinate label and no repeated field ID within a zoom crop.
protected_strengths: Every dot is a real, untinted, labelled Sentinel-2 field (coordinates and diameter) with visible rings, hubs, spokes and wedges at 10x
Oriented wedge/half-split fields rendering sub-dot edges: helmet rim, collar ring, flag stripes, canal and lake shorelines
Instant subject recognizability at 1x for both targets (face/patch/helmet/shuttle; lake lobes and canal)
High bank precision in Al Jawf, Columbia and Texas (100% of decided tiles) with tight circle fits
No visible repeated stamps within a zoom crop
Coherent desert-farm palette: colours stay plausible earth tones rather than synthetic
